title: Linkability of Student Submission Data
description: The student's assignment submission data (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) could be linked to their identity across different systems or time periods, potentially enabling academic profiling or tracking of their learning activities.

title: Identifiability of Student from Submission Data
description: The combination of student ID, course, and submission timestamp creates a unique identifier that could reveal the student's identity even if other data is anonymized, potentially exposing their academic record.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Assignment and Personal Data
description: The assignment work file and personal information (student ID, course) could be accessed by unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper access controls in the Grades Portal Web App.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Submission Data
description: The submission data (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted during transmission or storage within the Grades Portal Web App, potentially affecting academic assessment integrity.

title: Student Identity Usurpation for Assignment Submission
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the student to submit assignments or access their data through credential theft, session hijacking, or social engineering attacks against the Grades Portal Web App.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Submission Data
description: Student submission data including file references and course information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission from the Grades Portal Web App to the Assignment & Grading Service.
assumptions: Transmission channel lacks adequate encryption or access controls

title: Tampering with Grading Request Data
description: Grading request data including student ID, course, and file reference could be altered during transmission, potentially affecting grade integrity.
assumptions: Data in transit is not properly authenticated or integrity-protected

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grading Results
description: The Assignment & Grading Service could expose grading results to unauthorized users or systems, violating student privacy expectations.
assumptions: Service lacks proper access controls and role-based authorization

title: Student Identification from Grading Data
description: Student IDs combined with course and file reference information could be used to identify individual students, potentially enabling profiling or tracking.
assumptions: Student IDs are not properly anonymized or pseudonymized

title: Linkability of Submission Records
description: Submission records containing student ID, course, and file reference could be linked across multiple submissions or with other data sources, creating comprehensive student profiles.
assumptions: Data is not properly segmented or isolated between contexts

title: Grade Manipulation by Authorized Personnel
description: Authorized personnel with access to the Assignment & Grading Service could potentially manipulate grading data without proper audit trails.
assumptions: Insufficient audit logging and access controls exist

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignment Data
description: Assignment files, student IDs, course information, and submission times stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: Datastore lacks proper encryption, access controls, or audit logging

title: Student Identification from Assignment Records
description: Student IDs stored in the assignment datastore enable direct identification of students, potentially allowing tracking of academic activities without consent.
assumptions: Student IDs are not anonymized or pseudonymized

title: Linkability of Assignment Data to Other Records
description: Student IDs and course information in DS1 could be linked with other student records (e.g., grades, personal data) to create comprehensive profiles.
assumptions: Other student data systems exist and are interconnected

title: Excessive Data Collection in Assignment Submission
description: Storing full assignment files along with metadata (student ID, course, submission time) may exceed what is necessary for grading purposes.
assumptions: Full file storage is required for academic integrity verification

title: Student Identity Usurpation During Submission
description: Without proper authentication, students could submit assignments under another student's identity, compromising academic integrity and privacy.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are not robust

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Student Data Storage
description: Storing student identification and academic data may violate FERPA, GDPR, or other privacy regulations if proper safeguards are not implemented.
assumptions: Institution has privacy compliance obligations

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Grades
description: Student grades and submission data could be disclosed to unauthorized teachers, students, or external parties through the Grades Portal Web App, violating student privacy and confidentiality expectations.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or authentication mechanisms in the web application

title: Student Identification Through Grades
description: Students could be identified from their grades and submission patterns, potentially revealing personal information about their academic performance and course enrollment.
assumptions: Grades are displayed in a way that allows identification of individual students

title: Teacher Identity Impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate a teacher to access grades and submission queues, potentially viewing or manipulating student data without authorization.
assumptions: Weak authentication or session management in the login process

title: Linkability of Teacher and Student Data
description: Teacher identity could be linked to specific student submissions and grades, creating a comprehensive profile of teacher-student interactions that may be sensitive.
assumptions: System logs or metadata record which teacher accessed which student submissions

title: Excessive Data Collection on Submissions
description: The system may collect more data than necessary for grade review, such as detailed submission metadata, timestamps, or ancillary information not required for the core function.
assumptions: Data collection policies are not aligned with data minimization principles

title: Student Identifiability via Submission Data
description: Student names and work content in submissions could identify individual students to unauthorized parties if teacher access is compromised or if data is intercepted during transmission.
assumptions: Teacher account credentials are protected; data transmission is encrypted.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Submissions
description: Student work content, names, and submission times could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through teacher account compromise, insider threats, or system vulnerabilities in the portal.
assumptions: Teacher has legitimate access; system has basic security controls.

title: Linkability of Student Submissions
description: Submission times combined with student names and work content could link multiple submissions to specific students, potentially revealing patterns or enabling cross-referencing with other data sources.
assumptions: Teacher has access to all submission data; no additional linking data is available.

title: Educational Privacy Regulation Non-Compliance
description: Displaying student names and work content to teachers may violate FERPA or similar educational privacy regulations if proper consent, access controls, or data minimization measures are not implemented.
assumptions: Applicable privacy regulations require specific handling of student data.

title: Student and Teacher Identifiability
description: The data flow includes student ID and grader ID fields that could be used to identify specific students and teachers. Even with anonymization, the combination of these identifiers with grades and feedback could potentially re-identify individuals.
assumptions: Student and teacher IDs are not properly anonymized or pseudonymized before storage

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grades and Feedback
description: Grades and written feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the Grades Portal Web App lacks proper access controls. This could lead to privacy violations for students and teachers.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or enforced

title: Grade and Feedback Manipulation
description: Grades and feedback text could be altered by unauthorized users or even by the teacher after submission, compromising data integrity and fairness in the grading process.
assumptions: Input validation and audit logging are not properly implemented

title: Linkability Across Data Sources
description: The combination of student ID, grader ID, grade, and feedback could be linked with other data sources (e.g., student records, teacher profiles) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals, potentially revealing sensitive patterns.
assumptions: Other data sources exist that could be linked with this flow's data

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Grading Actions
description: Teachers may be able to deny submitting grades or feedback after the fact, which could lead to disputes and undermine the integrity of the grading system.
assumptions: No audit trail or digital signature mechanism is in place

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records contain sensitive personal information including student IDs, grades, and feedback. Unauthorized access by malicious actors or compromised system accounts could lead to privacy violations and potential discrimination based on academic performance.
assumptions: System has inadequate access controls or authentication mechanisms

title: Data Leakage Through System Logs
description: Grade data may be inadvertently logged in system audit trails, error logs, or debug information, creating unauthorized disclosure vectors for sensitive student information.
assumptions: Logging mechanisms capture full grade record details

title: Grade Record Loss Due to System Failure
description: Grade records could be permanently lost due to database corruption, hardware failure, or software bugs, resulting in loss of academic records and potential inability to verify student performance history.
assumptions: No adequate backup or disaster recovery mechanisms in place

title: Student Identification Through Grade Data Correlation
description: Student IDs combined with course information and grades could be used to identify specific students, especially when correlated with other publicly available data, potentially deanonymizing students.
assumptions: Grade data is accessible to unauthorized parties

title: Lack of Audit Trail for Grade Modifications
description: Without comprehensive audit trails, it may be impossible to prove who modified a grade, when, and why, leading to potential grade tampering without accountability.
assumptions: System lacks immutable logging of all grade-related operations

title: Unauthorized Grade Modification
description: Malicious actors with system access could alter grades without proper authorization, affecting student records and academic integrity.
assumptions: Insufficient access controls or authentication for grade modification operations

title: Grading Service Unavailability
description: The Assignment & Grading Service could become unavailable due to system overload, maintenance, or attacks, preventing legitimate grading activities and delaying grade distribution.
assumptions: No adequate redundancy or failover mechanisms

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper sharing mechanisms in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or enforced; data is transmitted or stored without adequate encryption.

title: Unauthorized Access via Identity Impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate a student to access their grades and feedback through credential theft, phishing, or weak authentication mechanisms.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are not sufficiently robust; students may reuse passwords or fall victim to social engineering.

title: Grade Data Tampering and Modification
description: Grades and feedback could be altered, deleted, or corrupted by unauthorized actors or system errors, compromising data integrity and academic records.
assumptions: Input validation and integrity checks are insufficient; system lacks proper audit trails for grade modifications.

title: Linkability of Grades to Student Identity
description: Student grades could be linked to their identity in ways that create privacy risks, such as enabling profiling or tracking of academic performance over time.
assumptions: Grades are stored with identifiable information; no anonymization or pseudonymization is applied.

title: Student Identification from Grades Data
description: Individual students could be identified from their grades data, potentially revealing sensitive information about academic performance, learning patterns, or institutional affiliation.
assumptions: Grades data contains or can be combined with identifying information; data is not properly anonymized.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades and teacher feedback
description: The Grades Portal Web App may transmit student grades and teacher feedback to unauthorized parties if proper access controls, authentication, and encryption mechanisms are not implemented. This could expose sensitive academic information to malicious actors or unauthorized personnel.

title: Linkability of student grades with other personal data
description: Student grades and teacher feedback could be linked with other personal information about the student (e.g., name, ID, course enrollment), potentially creating a comprehensive profile that reveals sensitive information about the student's academic performance and capabilities.

title: Identification of student through grade data
description: If the grade data includes identifying information or is displayed in a way that allows identification (e.g., with student name, ID, or unique course combinations), unauthorized parties could identify the student and potentially target them for harassment or discrimination.

title: Excessive data sharing beyond necessity
description: The portal may share more student data than necessary for the intended purpose of displaying grades and feedback. This could include unnecessary personal identifiers or detailed feedback that exceeds what is needed for the student to understand their academic standing.

title: Unauthorized Account Access
description: Parent's account credentials could be compromised, allowing unauthorized parties to access the parent's account and request grades for their child.
assumptions: Parent uses weak password or credentials are intercepted during transmission

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Grades
description: Child's grades could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through insecure data transmission or improper access controls in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without encryption or access controls are insufficient

title: Child Identifiability from Grades Data
description: Grades data could be used to identify the specific child, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's academic performance and identity.
assumptions: Grades are associated with identifiable information or can be cross-referenced with other data

title: Insecure Data Storage of Grades
description: Child's grades stored in the Grades Portal Web App could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems due to inadequate security measures.
assumptions: Data storage lacks proper encryption or access controls

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Academic Data
description: Child's grades, feedback, and submission history could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through insecure transmission or improper access controls in the Grades Portal Web App.

title: Linkability of Academic Data with Other Records
description: The child's academic data could be linked with other personal information or school records, creating a comprehensive profile that exceeds the intended scope of the data sharing.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grades Portal
description: Unauthorized individuals could access the Grades Portal Web App and view sensitive academic information about the child, including grades and submission history.

title: Improper Identification of Authorized Parent
description: The system may fail to properly verify that the parent accessing the data is the authorized guardian, potentially allowing unauthorized family members or others to access the child's academic records.

title: Misrepresentation of Academic Performance
description: The grades, feedback, or submission history displayed to the parent could be inaccurate, outdated, or manipulated, leading to incorrect understanding of the child's academic standing.
uncertainty_note: Less certain - depends on data integrity controls

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student/Parent Personal Information
description: The Grades Portal Web App may expose sensitive personal information (names, emails, roles, relationships) to unauthorized users through improper access controls or data leakage in the web interface.

title: Malicious Modification of Account Data
description: An authorized administrator could maliciously modify student/parent account data, roles, or parent-child relationships, leading to data integrity issues and potential misuse of information.

title: Identification of Students/Parents Through Portal
description: Unauthorized parties could identify specific students or parents by accessing the portal and viewing account information, relationships, or role assignments.

title: Administrator Account Compromise
description: The School Administrator account could be compromised through credential theft or session hijacking, allowing unauthorized access to create, modify, or disable accounts and parent-child links.

title: Lack of Audit Trail for Administrative Actions
description: Administrative actions (creating, modifying, disabling accounts) may not be properly logged, making it difficult to establish non-repudiation and accountability for data changes.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Account Records
description: The Assignment & Grading Service writes account records to the Account Directory. An attacker could intercept or manipulate this data flow to modify account information, potentially altering student records, grades, or parent-child relationships.
assumptions: The data flow is not adequately protected against interception or manipulation during transmission to the datastore.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Parent-Child Relationship Links
description: The grading service writes parent-child relationship links to the account directory. An attacker could modify these relationships to create false familial connections or sever legitimate ones, potentially affecting access controls or inheritance-based permissions.
assumptions: Parent-child relationship data is sensitive and requires protection from unauthorized modification.

title: Linkability of Account Records via Parent-Child Relationships
description: Parent-child relationship links written to the account directory could be used to link different account records together, potentially revealing family relationships between individuals who may not expect their connections to be discoverable.
assumptions: The parent-child relationship data is not anonymized or pseudonymized before storage.

title: Identification of Individuals via Account Records
description: Account records written to the directory contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify individuals, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Account records contain sufficient PII to enable identification.

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Account Record Writes
description: When the grading service writes account records to the directory, there may be no audit trail or cryptographic proof to prevent denial of actions taken, making it difficult to verify who made changes to records.
assumptions: The system does not implement proper audit logging or digital signatures for write operations.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Student Data
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transmitted to third-party cloud hosting provider, creating risk of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal and educational information to unauthorized parties within or outside the provider's organization.
assumptions: Cloud provider has inadequate access controls or insider threats exist

title: Data Tampering During Transmission
description: Nightly database backup and replication data could be intercepted or modified in transit to the cloud hosting provider, compromising data integrity of grades and assignments.
assumptions: Transmission encryption may be insufficient or compromised

title: Unauthorized Access by Cloud Provider Personnel
description: Cloud hosting provider employees or contractors may have unauthorized access to full student records, grades, and account directory information stored on their infrastructure.
assumptions: Cloud provider lacks proper role-based access controls or audit mechanisms

title: Identification of Students Through Account Directory
description: Account directory data transmitted to cloud provider contains personally identifiable information that could be used to identify individual students and their educational records.
assumptions: Account directory contains sufficient PII to identify individuals

title: Linkability of Student Records Across Systems
description: Combination of grades, assignments, and account directory data could be linked across different systems or time periods to create comprehensive profiles of students, potentially enabling re-identification or profiling.
assumptions: Data is not properly anonymized or pseudonymized before transmission

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Data Transmission
description: Difficulty in proving the origin and authenticity of data transmitted to cloud provider, making it challenging to establish accountability for data handling and potential breaches.
assumptions: No cryptographic signing or audit trail exists for data transfers

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records database contains sensitive personal information about students, parents, and teachers. Unauthorized access could expose private academic performance data, potentially leading to discrimination, bullying, or other harms.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or are bypassed

title: Student Identification from Grade Records
description: Grade records can be used to identify individual students, potentially revealing their academic standing, special needs, or other sensitive information that could be misused.
assumptions: Grade records contain identifiable information that can be correlated with student identities

title: Linkability of Grade Data with Other Information
description: Grade records could be linked with other data sources (e.g., attendance records, behavioral data, demographic information) to create comprehensive profiles of students, parents, and teachers without their consent.
assumptions: Other data sources exist that could be correlated with grade records

title: Excessive Data Collection for Multiple Views
description: The grading service builds student, parent, and teacher views, potentially collecting and processing more data than necessary for each specific view, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: All grade records are processed for all views regardless of necessity

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk for Educational Data
description: Grade records may be subject to educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA in the US, GDPR in Europe). Improper handling could result in regulatory violations and legal consequences.
assumptions: The system operates under jurisdictions with educational data protection regulations
